title: Example: documentation access changed for agent workflows
summary: Prototype signal showing how a material API or integration change would be summarized after snapshot comparison and source verification.
whyItMatters: A documentation provider sits directly in the context path of coding agents, so interface changes can alter reliability across every downstream run.

title: Example: a pricing or allowance change crossed the threshold
summary: Prototype record for a pricing-page diff. The live engine will attach captured before/after evidence instead of relying on vendor copy.
whyItMatters: Review automation is often embedded in team workflows; a material price or allowance change can affect the economics of every repository using it.

title: Example: browser testing gained a workflow-relevant capability
summary: Prototype signal representing a release that materially changes what can be automated, while cosmetic release-note churn would be dropped.
whyItMatters: A meaningful browser-testing capability can remove repeated manual QA work; a renamed button cannot. The materiality filter exists to separate the two.

title: Example: a security or data-handling policy changed
summary: Prototype evidence type for terms, privacy or data-handling changes that can matter more than a visible product feature.
whyItMatters: Security tooling may inspect sensitive repositories. Policy changes deserve a different level of scrutiny than ordinary UI updates.

title: Example: the underlying AI behaviour changed in a research workflow
summary: Prototype signal for a model or analysis-layer update whose effect should be checked against source material rather than trusted from marketing language.
whyItMatters: Research synthesis is only useful when evidence remains inspectable; a model change matters when it changes how claims are produced or traced.

title: Example: a new workflow entered the watchset but did not merit P0
summary: Prototype record showing that discovery and publication are separate. A new capability can be tracked without being promoted as must-know news.
whyItMatters: The value of Should Know is the rejection layer: discovery can be broad while the public feed remains deliberately narrow.
